summary: Rust nat candidate with verified full-build reuse, explicit complete/incomplete responses, retained rejection diagnostics, legacy full-response compatibility, and unchanged scoped authority rules. Includes offline CLI/schema fixtures for reuse, drift, rejection, and existing CLI behavior. A read-only comparison of the previous six-file candidate measured 108,286 fewer response bytes (87.78%) with all-null reuse; this is not a live token or timing measurement. Generated software and checks were not executed.

requirements.statement: Provide a nat executable with init, build, watch, run, test, status, check, and promote commands and the documented command shapes and flags.
Support help/--help/-h and version/--version/-V; reject invalid commands, options, missing values, and excess arguments with useful diagnostics and nonzero status.

Except for init, discover projects by searching the current directory and ancestors for spec/, or require DIR/spec for explicit --project DIR; interpret relative flag paths from the caller's directory.

init defaults to the current directory, creates spec/, inferred/, and generated/, preserves existing .nat sources, creates a greeting-by-name starter defaulting to the world only if no .nat files exist, and prints the project and next step.

Under Commands, build validates and writes compilation results, skips the compiler only when inputs and tracked artifacts are current and no explicit proposal is given, always loads and validates an explicitly selected --proposal JSON even on a current build, and supports --full to force whole-project rebuilding.
run builds as needed and executes the generated argv from generated/, forwarding remaining arguments literally and honoring -- as the end of nat option parsing.
test builds as needed, executes every generated check from generated/, and fails when checks are absent or any check fails.

status reports absent builds, stale inputs, edited or missing tracked artifacts, or current builds, including the previous summary and file counts; check succeeds only when all tracked sources, references, generated files, and inferred files match.

watch performs a startup build/check, polls approximately every 150 ms, rebuilds approximately 400 ms after the last input change, runs checks unless --no-test is supplied, and continues after build or check errors.

promote accepts an existing assumption only from a current build, appends its statement to spec/promoted.nat, removes the inferred assumption, and updates the manifest so check passes without silently overwriting other sources.
Record per-spec input hashes including direct references and per-output source dependencies, and verify tracked outputs before every rebuild.

Scope existing-source changes only when dependency metadata is complete and at least one but not all outputs are affected; added/removed sources, missing metadata, or all affected outputs require full compilation.
Scoped input includes only changed specs, relevant prior semantic records, affected output contents, prior dependency metadata, run/check commands, and IDs reserved by unchanged specs.
Scoped responses replace changed-source semantic records and replace or explicitly remove every affected output, may add outputs, and provide complete updated commands and summary.

Reject scoped changes to unaffected outputs or unchanged-source semantic records, validate unique IDs, paths, dependencies and commands after merging, preserve unaffected files, and fall back to full compilation before writes for invalid scoped responses or wider effects.

Use shared freshness and rebuild logic for build, watch, run, and test; unchanged builds without explicit proposals never invoke Codex, --full always compiles the whole project, and linked-file edits change every directly referring spec.
Implement a small local compiler loop as a Cargo-installable Rust CLI named nat for macOS and Linux with a small dependency set; generated applications may use other languages.
Treat spec/**/*.nat as authoritative human intent, inferred/assumptions.inat as reviewable replaceable inference, and generated/ as disposable code, checks, semantic records, and manifest.
Support overriding inferred behavior through source edits or assumption promotion, and require human changes to generated behavior to be expressed in specs.
A fresh nat init hello followed by nat run in the project compiles and runs a greeting; help documents all supported commands and flags.
Compile these specs into a separate generated Rust crate with binary nat and meaningful checks covering initialization, full/scoped builds, drift, and CLI behavior.
Execute generated programs and checks from generated/ using argument arrays without shell interpolation, stream output and diagnostics, and treat nonzero exits as errors.

When run fails for a missing executable, interpreter module, native library, or GUI display dependency, report 'recompiling for this machine', send the failure to Codex for one full recompilation, validate and run replacement checks, then retry once with the original arguments.
Report ordinary runtime failures without regeneration and prevent repeated repair loops.

Explain in CLI help and README that compilation has read-only workspace access but generated programs and checks execute with the user's local privileges; do not silently select or execute saved proposals.

Provide meaningful tests without live Codex calls for initialization, forwarding, full/scoped/no-op builds, old manifests, drift refusal, source/reference staleness, promotion, watching, and runtime dependency repair.
Treat the repository root spec/ as canonical and produce a generated/ Rust crate with Cargo manifest, binary nat, and cargo test --offline or an equivalent reliable check.

Keep the handwritten bootstrap and generated candidate separate until the candidate implements the specified CLI and build protocol and passes parity checks; do not overwrite the running compiler during its own build.
Document bootstrap installation and candidate build, testing, comparison, and installation, clearly identifying which runner each Cargo command installs.

Allow rebuilding from .nat sources and installed Codex without treating bootstrap Rust code as authoritative, and refuse to replace directly edited generated artifacts until edits are moved into specs or discarded.
The generated Rust crate, including test targets, must compile, pass tests, and pass Clippy with warnings denied.
Generated tests obey Rust borrowing rules: bind a vector element once before mutating multiple fields rather than taking overlapping mutable borrows through separate indexed expressions.
Give each generated file the smallest accurate set of .nat dependencies to enable subsequent scoped rebuilds; list all specs only for files genuinely depending on all specs.

Read UTF-8 Markdown and plain-prose .nat files recursively beneath spec/, requiring at least one source and using exact spec-relative paths with slash separators in records; keep citations in statements or reasons rather than source paths.
Resolve direct Markdown links and images relative to the containing .nat file and track linked local file bytes without following references recursively.
Do not fetch or track remote URLs, email links, same-document anchors, or raw HTML references.
Reject missing local files, references escaping the project or entering generated/ or inferred/, and all symlinks within spec/; reference errors identify the source and failed destination.
Treat linked content as supporting context rather than instructions overriding human .nat intent.
Read sources and reference hashes deterministically, detect source additions/removals/edits and reference changes, and avoid compiler calls for unchanged inputs.

Under Local references, canonicalize both the project root and each target before checking containment, accept macOS /var and /private/var aliases of the same project, preserve stable project-relative reference keys, and test ordinary and nested-spec references through an aliased project root.

Invoke the installed authenticated Codex CLI from the project root with read-only workspace access and structured JSON output; pass absolute paths for -o and --output-schema. Only the Rust runner writes generated and inferred artifacts.

Surface compiler failures and diagnostics, suppress successful normal transcripts and submitted source text, immediately announce full or scoped compilation counts, and periodically report elapsed compilation time.

Full compilation receives every source's original Markdown and direct reference hashes, plus previous inference and semantic records. Require read-only runtime inspection, explicit product assumptions, minimal implementation, and meaningful checks.

Return structured summary, requirements, assumptions, files, run, and checks. Files identify every direct and indirect .nat dependency. Full responses contain a complete inventory with string content or verified null reuse; scoped responses retain full string content. Commands are argv arrays executed from generated/ without an implicit shell, and an empty run denotes a non-runnable project.

Constrain schema sources to exact supplied paths and independently validate saved proposals for nonempty valid unique semantic IDs, mapped requirements, existing sources, unique output paths, dependencies, and argv values.
Reject generated paths that escape, traverse symlinks, collide with parent files, or use reserved ir.json or .nat-manifest.json paths; reject empty argv elements.
Validate the whole result and verify tracked generated and inferred artifacts before writing; refuse edited or deleted tracked artifacts and untracked overwrites.

Render semantic records and reviewable inferred assumptions with exact Source: spec/<path> labels and complete reasons. Record hashes, commands, dependencies, and summary in the manifest; remove omitted full-result outputs and avoid rewriting unchanged bytes.

Accept omitted sources in legacy full files with string content, conservatively attributing them to every current source. New compiler schemas require sources, and scoped responses require explicit dependencies.
Invalid semantic ID or source diagnostics identify the record kind and ID, such as invalid assumption A-01 or source.

Both compiler scopes explicitly state that .nat files are Markdown and require viewing referenced images read-only. Scoped input supplies changed sources and affected old output contents while omitting unrelated source and output contents.

Before full compilation, freeze verified prior tracked output bytes and advertise a compact catalog of exact relative paths, hashes, and dependencies. Permit local inspection without narrowing semantic scope or dependencies to reduce response size.

Resolve full-response null content exclusively from the frozen advertised catalog. Require exact tracked paths and current explicit dependencies; refuse fresh-build, missing, untracked, unadvertised, wrong-case, duplicate, symlinked, or stale reuse without publishing artifacts.

Validate the fully assembled result under ordinary structural rules and recheck source, manifest, and prior artifact hashes immediately before publication. Reused files retain exact bytes and are not rewritten; omitted files retain ordinary full-build deletion semantics.

For explicitly imported full proposals, freeze and verify the current tracked build at invocation as the reuse basis and report that basis in diagnostics. Preserve legacy string proposals and the existing scoped protocol.

New full schemas require status complete or incomplete and a diagnostic string. Reject incomplete responses before artifact application, even when they contain plausible files and commands, preserve the prior build, and do not automatically retry compilation. Treat absent status in legacy full responses as legacy complete.

Retain rejected model responses outside generated/ and inferred/ and report their location. Complete status does not bypass structural validation or imply behavioral correctness. Never replace the installed compiler during self-regeneration.

Provide offline fixtures through the actual CLI and output-schema path covering partial and all-file reuse, unchanged metadata, executed declared checks, invalid reuse and concurrent drift, incomplete responses, and compatibility with legacy and scoped responses.
Measure response-byte savings using a real previous candidate and distinguish the offline encoding comparison from live token usage or wall-clock savings.
